ETYMOLOGIES.Definition: the origins and histories of words

ROOTS.Definition: origins; the places where something first came from

MUTINOUS.Definition: rebellious; refusing to obey those in charge

OBLITERATE.Definition: destroy completely so that nothing is left

PURISTS.Definition: people who want language to follow traditional rules exactly

EVOLVES.Definition: develops and changes slowly over time

GOBLIN.Definition: a small, ugly, evil creature in old stories

ETYMOLOGY.Definition: the origin and history of a word

RAVAGING.Definition: causing great damage and destruction across

SYMPTOMS.Definition: signs in the body that show someone has an illness

BACKSTORIES.Definition: stories about how something began or what happened before

LEGEND HAS IT.Definition: according to an old, popular story

ABBREVIATION.Definition: a short form of a longer word or phrase

DESIRABLE.Definition: attractive and wanted by many people

NORSE.Definition: the old language of Scandinavia, spoken by the Vikings

TRACE.Definition: follow something back to discover where it began

DEFINITIVE.Definition: final and certain, so that it settles the question

CONCRETE.Definition: real and certain, based on facts

HERMAPHRODITE.Definition: a person or animal with both male and female body parts

MAIDEN.Definition: an old word for a young unmarried woman

DAMSEL.Definition: an old-fashioned word for a young woman who is not married
